storyboard.claim: Saying I can't casts you as a victim of outside forces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bound by an outside force
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the sub-section on the psychology of the phrase I can't.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the abstract victim framing into a posture the viewer reads.
storyboard.staging: Bound by an outside force

storyboard.claim: A manager who hears I can't will simply remove the stated obstacle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss pointing at a task list while the everyman listens, the problem being reassigned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the victim framing backfires.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boss as the problem-solver who takes the excuse at face value.
storyboard.staging: The boss points at the task list and reassigns it: the excuse gets solved away.

storyboard.claim: I don't makes you the architect of your life, not a restriction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: I don't makes you the architect of your life.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts with the I can't victim posture just shown.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the agency concrete: the person is the one deciding.
storyboard.staging: I don't makes you the architect of your life.

storyboard.claim: I don't is a declaration of personal agency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman states a decision to the boss, finger pointed firmly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the donut example that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next example as a demonstration of agency.
storyboard.staging: Everyman states a decision to the boss, finger pointed firmly.

storyboard.claim: Saying I can't eat donuts implies a struggle against an impulse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A donut icon beside a worried everyman weighing the temptation in a break room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the donut example from the break room.
storyboard.addedInformation: The donut is the literal temptation; the worry shows the struggle.
storyboard.staging: Everyman, worried, looks at a donut icon: the struggle with the impulse is visible.

storyboard.claim: A coworker pushes you to break the diet you hate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The cheerful friend pointing with a plate of pressure while everyman hesitates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the impulse being pushed from outside.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the pressure a face: the friend nudges the everyman toward giving in.
storyboard.staging: The friend points at the treat, cheerful; everyman hesitates with a worried face.

storyboard.claim: I don't eat donuts is a declaration of identity, not a weakness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon and a calm everyman speaking the firm no.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the donut struggle into an identity statement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads as a protective boundary, which is the point of the no.
storyboard.staging: A shield beside a calm everyman: the firm no protects who they are.

storyboard.claim: I don't applies to deep work and gym evenings, not just snacks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman refuses admin work, holding his gym plan.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the identity rule to professional boundaries.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes stand for the admin work that would take the gym evening.
storyboard.staging: Everyman refuses admin work, holding his gym plan.

storyboard.claim: The psychological empowerment of I don't is the framing the hosts now test.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking on an empty stage, presenting the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host commentary that raises the workplace objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pure commentary frame; no new claim beyond the question.
storyboard.staging: The narrator speaks to camera on the empty stage: this is the hosts' question.

storyboard.claim: Saying I don't to a boss in a corporate setting risks getting fired.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss, angry, pointing a warning finger as the threat of dismissal lands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the risk of blunt refusal to a superior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Narration says laid; the callout gives the intended meaning fired, ASR-corrected.
storyboard.staging: The boss points and looks angry: the reprisal risk is the threat.

storyboard.claim: I don't work past 6 p.m. sounds insubordinate to a boss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss speaking with an angry face, rejecting the blunt line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the boss reaction to the blunt refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry face carries the verdict the narration gives the sentence.
storyboard.staging: The boss talks with a stern, angry face: the blunt phrasing reads as defiance.

storyboard.claim: The book is not advocating professional suicide; the delivery gets adjusted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman weighs bluntness against the boss's power.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the risk raised by the boss reaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected phrase, so the viewer reads it as refused.
storyboard.staging: Everyman weighs bluntness against the boss's power.

storyboard.claim: A softer script: my policy is to dedicate my evenings to family.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman gently tells the boss his evenings belong to family.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the smoother phrasing for a VP.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout gives the script's gist in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Everyman gently tells the boss his evenings belong to family.

storyboard.claim: Even softened, the inner frame must move away from I can't.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman's polite surface hides a firm inner decision.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the inner framing after the external script.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks I can't as the phrase to drop, reading as rejected.
storyboard.staging: Everyman's polite surface hides a firm inner decision.

storyboard.claim: I can't stay late because my car pool leaves at six is a fragile excuse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman offers a weak car pool excuse while the friend waits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the fragile excuse with the boundary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Box marks the excuse as weak and external.
storyboard.staging: Everyman offers a weak car pool excuse while the friend waits.

storyboard.claim: A boundary built on core principles beats a circumstance the VP can dismantle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon beside a calm everyman speaking firmly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the fragile excuse with the principle-based boundary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads as a stable principle the VP cannot pay away.
storyboard.staging: The shield stands beside a calm everyman: the boundary rests on principle.

storyboard.claim: I don't is the ultimate accounting rule for time and energy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman hands over nothing: one fixed rule decides ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host recap of the rule just laid out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the rule as an accounting principle without drawing money.
storyboard.staging: Everyman hands over nothing: one fixed rule decides ahead.

storyboard.claim: A pre-declined transaction: any request of this type is refused automatically.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from any request to auto declined, the decision taken out of the moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the accounting rule into a structural flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Flow shows the decision happens before the request arrives.
storyboard.staging: The flow draws requests going straight to auto declined; the everyman stays neutral beside it.

storyboard.claim: Consequences of saying no must be faced realistically.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman braces as the neighbor frowns at the refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the rule to its consequences.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats on the costs of a no.
storyboard.staging: Everyman braces as the neighbor frowns at the refusal.

storyboard.claim: Even a polite soft decline can leave the other person profoundly upset.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss slumped and sad after the polite refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the other side of the consequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sad slump shows upset without making the boss a villain.
storyboard.staging: The boss slumps sadly: the polite decline still hurts them.

storyboard.claim: Setting emotional boundaries is the hardest part of the framework.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman clutches a shield, bracing for the hardest part.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition to the emotional boundaries section.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the emotional section as the hardest.
storyboard.staging: Everyman clutches a shield, bracing for the hardest part.

storyboard.claim: The emotional boundary scene hurts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sags, holding the hard letter of a role-play.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the aunt scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the emotional tone for the scene.
storyboard.staging: Everyman sags, holding the hard letter of a role-play.

storyboard.claim: A demanding aunt calls and insists you spend your day off driving.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holding a modern phone with a worried face on a weekend kitchen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the aunt scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: Phone is a modern smartphone, matching the call.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holds the phone with a worried face: the call demands the day off.

callout.text: It takes three hours each way

storyboard.claim: The drive is three hours each way to a minor gathering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon with everyman slumped beside it, dreading the drive.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details the cost of the aunt request.
storyboard.addedInformation: Road reads as the long drive.
storyboard.staging: A road beside a slumped everyman: the drive is the burden.

callout.text: A polite decline, not an excuse

storyboard.claim: You politely decline with a prior commitment to rest this weekend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman politely declines by phone and the line goes silent.
storyboard.onScreenText: A polite decline, not an excuse
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The polite decline in the aunt scenario.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout gives the spoken excuse-free reason.
storyboard.staging: Everyman politely declines by phone and the line goes silent.

storyboard.claim: Her silence and sigh signal disappointment and a guilt trip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman winces holding the phone as a sigh comes through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Her reaction to the decline.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the everyman bracing for the trip.
storyboard.staging: Everyman winces holding the phone as a sigh comes through.

storyboard.claim: She says family just isn't a priority for you anymore.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The relative jabs a finger: the guilt trip lands on Everyman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The guilt-trip line.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout quotes the accusation directly.
storyboard.staging: The relative jabs a finger: the guilt trip lands on Everyman.

storyboard.claim: The guilt trip is the voice of a master manipulator.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon beside a smirking figure controlling the scene.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the manipulation in the aunt's line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer reads as one person controlling others.
storyboard.staging: A smirking figure beside the puppeteer icon: the manipulation is the control.

storyboard.claim: The people pleaser's instinct is to backpedal to stop her pain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman reaches to take it back and say yes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the instinct behind the backpedal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the internal pull toward giving in.
storyboard.staging: Everyman reaches to take it back and say yes.

storyboard.claim: Separate your logical decision from her emotional response.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holds his decision steady, apart from her feelings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fix to the backpedal instinct.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the separation as the action.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holds his decision steady, apart from her feelings.

storyboard.claim: Separating your feelings from others' feelings is critical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two different people: Everyman points between his thoughts and theirs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the concept behind the separation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the term the viewer can note.
storyboard.staging: Two different people: Everyman points between his thoughts and theirs.

storyboard.claim: You must absolve yourself as the cause of their negative reactions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman clears himself of blame for their reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The strict position the author takes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout states the author's position in the author's own words.
storyboard.staging: Everyman clears himself of blame for their reaction.

storyboard.claim: The absolution argument is a hard pill to swallow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman grimaces, forcing down a hard truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host reaction to the strict position.
storyboard.addedInformation: Idiom staged as reluctance, not a literal medical pill.
storyboard.staging: Everyman grimaces, forcing down a hard truth.

storyboard.claim: Their anger, passive aggression and manipulation come from circumstances outside your control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss speaking with an angry face, showing the other side's anger.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the reactions that belong to them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reaction as theirs.
storyboard.staging: The boss talks angrily: the anger is theirs to own.

storyboard.claim: The reaction belongs to them, not you, though the host struggles with this.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman doubts, pointing to who owns the reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts' doubt about the absolution.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the struggle with the claim.
storyboard.staging: Everyman doubts, pointing to who owns the reaction.

callout.text: A nod would have pleased her

storyboard.claim: Had I said yes, my aunt would have been happy, so my no caused her distress.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman holds the car keys, picturing the happy aunt.
storyboard.onScreenText: A yes would have pleased her
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host's logical objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the counterfactual the host is weighing.
storyboard.staging: Everyman holds the car keys, picturing the happy aunt.

storyboard.claim: My no caused her distress; action A led to reaction B.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman protests that his refusal made her upset.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host's objection stated in full.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout restates the causal claim being challenged.
storyboard.staging: Everyman protests that his refusal made her upset.

storyboard.claim: There is a distinction between triggering an emotion and causing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator separates trigger from cause while Everyman listens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the distinction that answers the objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Callout names the distinction as the answer.
storyboard.staging: Narrator separates trigger from cause while Everyman listens.

storyboard.claim: Your no triggered her disappointment, but you did not cause her inability to handle it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with two buckets: your no and her reaction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The distinction applied to the aunt.
storyboard.addedInformation: Buckets split the trigger from the cause.
storyboard.staging: The sorter separates your no from her reaction; the everyman stays neutral beside it.

storyboard.claim: A securely attached adult can hear no without manipulation or guilt trips.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A calm adult hears refusal without guilt trips.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the aunt scenario with the healthy standard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the standard the viewer should expect of the other adult.
storyboard.staging: A calm adult hears refusal without guilt trips.
